title: Regular parameter fibre in a smooth polynomial algebra
statement: Let k be a field, A a commutative k-algebra, d a natural number and f:k[X_i | i∈Fin d]→A a k-algebra map whose affine spectrum morphism is smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Suppose A/J is nonzero, where J=(f(X_i)). Then A is nonzero regular Noetherian, (f(X_i)) is an A-regular sequence, A/J is regular Noetherian and smooth over k, and Spec(A/J)→Spec A is a regular closed immersion of constant codimension d. The empty sequence d=0 is allowed.

source.place: Algebra, Tags 00T4 and 00TA; Algebra, Tag 07NF; Divisors, Tags 063D and 063G; original node steps 7–8.

proof.text: The variables are a regular sequence in the polynomial ring: prefix quotients retain only the remaining variables and multiplication by the next variable is coefficientwise injective. Smoothness gives flatness. Tensor the multiplication injections with A, identifying the tensors with the prefix quotients of A. The nonzero final quotient upgrades weak regularity to regularity.

Evaluation at zero identifies the quotient of the polynomial ring by its variables with k. Smooth base change identifies A/(f(X_i)) as a smooth k-algebra. Polynomial rings over fields and fields are regular Noetherian, so regularity ascends to A and its quotient.

The quotient projection is surjective with kernel generated by the displayed length-d regular sequence. Use the full affine chart and its global-section identifications to obtain the regular closed immersion of constant codimension d. If d=0 the sequence is empty and this is the identity immersion.
